answer: In an agent economy, each voting identity must lock collateral, and voting weight is proportional to that stake. Splitting one deposit across a thousand bots therefore buys no extra influence. Cheap accounts offer no oasis: an attacker must acquire and immobilize real capital to gain power. A spiral of new identities cannot evade that cost; the defense rests on scarce collateral, even when identities are as plentiful as shale.
